originalFinding.trigger: Retain 32 managed worktrees under one execution identity, switch between native and Root while retaining the supervisor home, then create another worktree from a repository owned by the newly selected identity. Its new nativeHome can be below the helper-local limit while the shared supervisor managed_worktrees table is already full.
originalFinding.impact: The helper creates the new checkout before the shared capacity check rejects its positive acknowledgement. The witness transaction rolls back to unknown without a binding, so the new retained checkout cannot be read/attached through the managed worktree API and requires manual inspection. This unnecessarily exceeds the intended shared retention budget and enters activity uncertainty instead of a safe not_sent capacity rejection.
evidence: RuntimeWorkspace executes runWorkspace first (src/runtime/workspace-service.ts:61) and only then witness.complete (line 65). Its beforeWrite invokes boundary and witness.reserve; reserve validates only the witness-row budget, not managed-worktree capacity (src/runtime/workspace-witness.ts:66-79).

The shared managed_worktrees table is initialized from the supervisor witness DB, and its global count >=32 is checked only in WorktreeBindings.complete (src/runtime/worktree-bindings.ts:34-36), inside the post-ack transaction; failures roll that transaction back (src/runtime/workspace-witness.ts:107-119).

deploy/units.py:59-67,111-115 and deploy/execution_identity.py:31-36 select distinct worker/worker-root native homes but retain one supervisor home and DB. deploy/workspace_worktrees.py:79-89,264-296 checks only the selected native-home holders before physically creating the checkout and returning created:true.

.work/v230-round1-worktree-capacity-evidence.json: completedBindingsBeforeSwitch=32; reservePassed=true; completion={code:capacity,delivery:unknown}; witnessAfterCompletion.state=unknown; binding.code=worktree_unbound. The reproduction uses the actual WorkspaceWitness implementation, distinct project identities and simulated valid helper acknowledgements.

conclusion: The original cross-execution-identity managed-worktree capacity defect is repaired for these exact three file hashes. No remaining findings were identified in this incremental scope.

method.reading: Read both changed production modules and the entire changed test file. Rechecked the unchanged RuntimeWorkspace beforeWrite caller and runWorkspace stdin boundary to verify that a failed reserve cannot send the helper request.
method.ordering: Existing operation identity conflict/unknown checks precede capacity checks. Shared live bindings plus unresolved worktree/create reservations are checked before the witness INSERT and before stdin.end(body). Synchronous single-supervisor admission has no await between count and INSERT. The complete-stage defensive limit remains.
method.lifecycle: Completing a reservation atomically replaces its pending contribution with a managed binding. Acknowledgement deletes only completed witness rows, preserving bound slots. discardNotSent deletes only the exact unresolved operation identity and therefore releases only a proven-not-sent reservation. Non-create operations bypass the worktree slot check.
method.tests: Read the added cross-nativeHome restart / 32 acknowledged bindings / 32 unconfirmed reservations / exact not_sent release / ordinary mutation cases. Verified the supplied targeted JSON artifact records four passed test files and 29 passed tests; did not rerun that suite.

independentExecution.limitations: Valid helper acknowledgements are simulated; no actual Git worktree is created. Actual stdin-beforeWrite ordering was independently re-read. No deployment, personal credentials, commercial inference, external MCP or full suite was used.

preservation: Original round1 report and reproduction evidence remain unchanged. This repair review binds only the three explicit current hashes and does not silently replace the original manifest digest.
